title: feat(desktop): camera bubble shape and size controls
body:
## What changed

The camera toggle becomes configurable without weighing more (design "Kaipu Camera Controls", direction **1a: split toggle + popover**). Backlog doc: [Camera bubble — shape and size](apps/documentation/src/content/docs/backlog/camera-bubble-shape-and-size.md).

- **Setting.** `AppSettings.cameraBubble = { shape: "circle" | "rounded", size: 120–480, deviceId: string | null }`, default circle / 240 / OS default camera. Merged field by field over the defaults (`sanitizeCameraBubble` in `src/shared/camera-bubble.ts`; an out-of-range size is clamped, not dropped). It lives in `AppSettings` and not `RecordingSettings`, because `RecordingSettings` is in-memory only and shape and size have to persist.
- **Bubble window (main).** It follows `cameraBubble.size` live, mid-take included, and resizes from its anchored bottom-left corner, so it grows up and to the right. The window is the bubble plus a 24 px transparent pad (shadow, label, grip), 32 px from the edges, so the visible edge stays 56 px in, as before. **Drag removed:** the old `-webkit-app-region: drag` is gone and the window is now `movable: false`. The bubble is fixed at its corner and its position is not persisted.
- **Record page.** The Camera tile splits into the toggle body and a 28 px chevron, which opens a 272 px `role="dialog"` popover under the row.
- **Capture panel.** The same split tile (22 px chevron). It expands an inline drawer, so the panel grows downward and focus stays inside the window. Esc or the chevron closes it.
- **Content.** Shape radiogroup, Size chips S · M · L · Custom, a 120–480 slider with preset ticks, a device selector, the camera-off note, the live note (`aria-live="polite"`), and the blocked card with "Open System Settings".
- **Bubble hover chrome** (only when not recording): 2 px pink outline, a "240 px · M" label and a resize grip (a dot on the rim at 45° for Circle, an L at the corner for Rounded). The grip previews the resize through main (`previewCameraBubbleSize`, clamped to the area) and on release saves the size that is actually on screen. Once `activity.active` is true, none of the chrome renders, and a drag in progress is cancelled.
- **Device.** `enumerateDevices()` filtered to `videoinput`. The app had no camera enumeration before this. It never opens the camera just to read device labels. A remembered device that has been unplugged falls back to the default camera.
- **Wiring.** Only the camera tile changes, through a new `cameraSlot` on `RecordingToggles` (backed by a new `element` field on `@kaipu/ui` `StatusToggleRow` items). The panel gets one more line for the drawer under the row. Nothing else in either layout moves.

## Decisions taken without asking

1. **Blocked detection uses a new tri-state `getCameraAccessStatus()`** (`granted` / `blocked` / `unknown`), not `checkPermissions().camera`. The latter is `false` before the user was ever asked. Blocking on it would have made the camera impossible to turn on for a first-time user.
2. **An area too small for the chosen size shrinks the bubble to what fits.** It hides only when not even 120 px fits (area under 232 × 232). Before, any area under 304 px hid it. The spec's decision 6 now carries an implementation note saying so.
3. **Preview resolution raised from 320×240 to 640×480 (ideal).** A 480 px bubble is 960 physical px on Retina, and 320 px would look soft in the recording.
4. **Slider Shift-steps stop on a preset they would jump over**, so the screen reader always hears the preset name when the value crosses one ("announces the preset name when crossing one").
5. **The drawer is `role="region"`** and its chevron has no `aria-haspopup`, because it is inline and not a popup. The Record page chevron keeps `aria-haspopup="dialog"`.
6. **Device selector is a native `<select>`** styled as a chip.
7. **Lock icon in the blocked card.** The app has no fox-nocam illustration.
8. **No analytics change.** The app does not track camera toggles today.
9. **Not built (deferred, as the design says):** the right-click context menu on the bubble.

## How to verify manually

1. Record page: click the chevron. The popover opens under the row with focus on Shape. Tab goes Shape → Size → slider → device. Esc closes it and focus returns to the chevron. With the camera on, every change resizes or reshapes the bubble immediately.
2. Camera off: the chevron still opens the settings and shows "Camera is off. These apply when you turn it on."
3. Capture panel: the chevron expands the drawer, the panel grows, and the panel does **not** hide while you use the chips, the slider or the native device `<select>`. Esc closes the drawer.
4. During a recording (from the panel): the pink live note appears. Changes apply live and appear in the recorded file.
5. Bubble, not recording: hover shows the outline, label and grip. Dragging the grip resizes it without moving the bottom-left corner. After release the size persists across a camera off/on.
6. Bubble, recording: hovering shows nothing. The recorded video contains no outline, label or grip.
7. Area recording: a medium area shrinks the bubble, and an area under 232 px hides it.
8. Deny camera in System Settings → Privacy → Camera, then refocus the app. The tile reads BLOCKED and cannot turn on. The settings show the blocked card, and its button opens the pane.

## What I could not verify

I could not run the Electron app with a camera here, so **none of the manual checks above were run**. In particular these are unverified:
- that hover events reach the inactive, always-on-top bubble window on macOS and Windows;
- that pointer capture during a grip drag stays smooth while the window resizes under the pointer;
- that the native `<select>` popup does not blur and hide the capture panel;
- the visual match with the design file, which I did not open; I worked from the written summary.

## Checks run

- `bun run test` in `apps/kaipu-record`: 273 files, 2425 tests passed.
- `packages/ui` tests: 98 passed. `packages/i18n` tests: 22 passed.
- `bun run verify:local` (lint, `oxfmt --check`, package builds, `check-types`): passed. The pre-push hook passed as well.

New tests cover settings defaults and merge, size clamping and preset mapping, the slider's step and snap behaviour, area fitting and the fixed corner, window not movable, live re-placement and the grip preview, the hub's settings listener, radiogroup and slider keyboard behaviour, Tab order, the blocked tile and card, popover open/close with focus return and outside press, drawer open/close, write throttling, and hover chrome hidden during a recording.
